D4.evidence: model/README.md I3; model/Lease-grantor-excerpt.tla Definitions Elect (guard ~\E l \in Nodes : IsLeader(l) /\ Connected(n, l)) and GrantTo (guard \A q \in Q : up[q] /\ Connected(l, q) /\ term[q] <= term[l]); traces/model-H3-tlc-counterexample.txt States 2, 6, 7, 11, 16, 20-22 (and corresponding records in traces/model-H3-counterexample.jsonl); traces/impl-H3-seed1.jsonl lines 2, 5, 6, 10, 14-15 (proc c1 seq 4 -> proc n1 seq 2 Grant token 3 in grantor_term 4).
D4.reasoning: In H3, n3 is elected leader in term 1 (State 2) and grants token 1 to c1 (State 4). Step 2 partitions {n3, c1, s} from {n1, n2, c2} (State 6). On the majority side {n1, n2}, n2 is elected in term 2 (State 7: term = [n1 |-> 2, n2 |-> 2, n3 |-> 1], lead = [n1 |-> 0, n2 |-> 2, n3 |-> 1]) and grants token 2 to c2 (State 9). Because n3 was not in {n1, n2}, it retains lead[n3] = 1 and term[n3] = 1. When the partition heals in State 11, n3 does not step down because of model choice I3 ('Nodes do not step down on learning a higher term'). When step 6 crashes the latest grantor n2 (State 16), the surviving live lease majority is {n1, n3} with term[n1] = 2, lead[n1] = 0 and term[n3] = 1, lead[n3] = 1. After c1 issues its final Request (State 20, want[c1] = TRUE), the model deadlocks (State 21 -> State 22 Stuttering): GrantTo(n3, c1) is disabled because the only live quorum {n1, n3} violates term[n1] <= term[n3] (2 <= 1), while Elect(n, {n1, n3}) is disabled for both n1 and n3 because ~\E l \in Nodes : IsLeader(l) /\ Connected(n, l) is blocked by the connected stale leader n3 (IsLeader(n3) is still true). In the implementation (impl-H3-seed1.jsonl), Raft steps down stale leaders / runs a new election in term 4 between the surviving nodes {n1, n2} after n3 crashes, granting token 3 to c1.
D4.same_class_as_M1_P10: Different stale-leadership mechanism (the inverse term relationship between surviving leader and follower). In M1's P10, a current (highest-term) leader elected by a 2-of-3 quorum could not bring a lagging (lower-term) follower into its term after its quorum partner crashed, yet blocked new elections. Current GrantTo fixes that case by allowing a leader l to grant across any quorum Q with term[q] <= term[l] and updating term[q] to term[l]. In H3, by contrast, the highest-term leader (n2, term 2) is the node that crashes (State 16), leaving a deposed lower-term leader (n3, term 1, lead 1) paired with a higher-term follower (n1, term 2, lead 0). Because nodes never step down on learning a higher term (I3), IsLeader(n3) remains true after heal (State 11), which simultaneously blocks Elect(n, {n1, n3}) via ~\E l \in Nodes : IsLeader(l) /\ Connected(n, l) and cannot satisfy GrantTo's term[q] <= term[l] (since term[n1] = 2 > term[n3] = 1).
D4.what_would_settle_it: The explained(model) verdict would be overturned only if the contract or failure model permitted a deposed minority leader to permanently suppress elections among a connected live majority containing a higher-term follower after the partition heals, or if the model still violated C1_4 on H3 when deposed leaders step down upon connectivity with a higher-term node (or when Elect only treats a connected leader l with term[l] >= term[n] / capable of forming a valid quorum as blocking elections).
